highlights.title: Nvidia Makes $3.5 Billion Bet on MediaTek
highlights.description: Nvidia is investing $3.5 billion in MediaTek, deepening collaboration with the Taiwanese chipmaker as it's working to persuade more companies to build chips that plug into its dominant data center ecosystem. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and MediaTek CEO Rick Tsai join Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow in this exclusive interview to discuss the deal. (Source: Bloomberg)

business.description: George Arison is done letting Wall Street's "Grindr discount" go unchallenged — in a wide-ranging Q&A, the CEO walks us through how AI, a controversial $350-plus EDGE tier, and a bet on healthcare and long-distance matchmaking are turning Grindr into the "gayborhood in your pocket" he's been promising since 2022.

business.title: Singapore Plans $173 Million in Fintech Funding Over Three Years
business.description: Singapore has earmarked S$220 million ($173 million) over three years to fund financial technology and innovation, as it seeks to stay competitive with other rival hubs including Hong Kong that are also investing in this area.

ev_autonomous.title: Tesla confirms Autopilot/FSD was active in strange fatal crash
ev_autonomous.description: Tesla told federal regulators that its driver-assist system was “verified engaged” when a Model 3 crashed at 104 mph and killed its driver in Clute, Texas — a detail that never appeared in any police statement or news report about the crash, which happened in May 2026. The gap between Tesla’s own data and the public account of the crash is the latest example of how little the public learns about crashes involving the company’s Autopilot and “Full Self-Driving” systems. more…

devices.title: Here’s the likely reason the iPhone Ultra isn’t getting an Apple Pencil
devices.description: A report yesterday suggested that Apple considered making a special version of the Apple Pencil for the upcoming iPhone Ultra before deciding against it. Bloomberg suggests that there are three reasons behind this decision, one of them being a desire not to conflict with the position adopted by Steve Jobs when launching the original iPhone. However, this was almost certainly not the deciding factor … more…

other.title: Polish Intelligence Probes Fire at Top Drone Firm WB Electronics
other.description: Poland’s security services are investigating whether a fire at a facility belonging to the country’s largest drone producer WB Electronics SA was an act of sabotage.
